newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW - short term shifts seen from next week. [CORRECTED 13:33 GMT]
newsitem.headline: VW - short term shifts seen from next week. [CORRECTED 13:33 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects the headline and the text to show when the short shifts are to begin.)
German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Friday that workers at the group's main plant in Wolfsburg would work shortened shifts from next week because of transport strikes in Spain.

Volkswagen became Germany's third carmaker affected by the nine-day old Spanish truckers strike, which has clogged Spanish roads and petrol stations preventing supplies from reaching their destinations.

The group said that it has suspended all special shifts in order to try and keep the plant open on Monday and that it has made a precautionary request at unemployment offices to pay out compensation to workers whose shifts will be pared back.
Volkswagen said the strike had choked off access to parts for its Polo and A3 models.

Earlier this morning Daimler-Benz AG said the strike had affected its plant in Vitoria, Spain where some 625 vehicles could not be built but that the impact had not yet affected operations in Germany.
Two days ago, Adam Opel AG, a unit of General Motors said it would interrupt production of its Vectra model at its Ruesselsheim plant from today.
BMW said on Friday that it had not yet been affected by the strike but was anticipating promblems if it goes on much longer.
